title: Provision RDS Subnet Group
scenario: Your platform team needs RDS Subnet Group for database placement across private subnets. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_db_subnet_group.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_db_subnet_group resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_db_subnet_group.

hints.why: Managed databases carry availability, backup and network requirements. Terraform makes those choices reviewable before a database is created.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_db_subnet_group. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a managed database service when you need backups, failover and patching handled by the provider rather than by an operator.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; tags; subnet_ids. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.subnet_group_name`, `var.project_name`, `var.environment`, `var.subnet_ids`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
